newsitem.title: GREECE: Greek depo, forward curves up, bonds idle, ecu/drs up.
newsitem.headline: Greek depo, forward curves up, bonds idle, ecu/drs up.

text.p: Greece's interbank depo and forex forwards were trading higher around mid-session, bonds were idling and ecu/drachma was firmer, trading around 309.50, dealers said.
"The forward and depo curves are up," said a dealer at a foreign bank. "Short-rates have increased about 30 basis points and long-tenors about a fourth of a point."
The trader attributed the rise in rates to tighter liquidity and uncertainty about the amount of 14-day funds the central bank would absorb today.
The Bank of Greece offered to drain an unspecified amount of 14-day funds at 11.90 percent in its regular fixed rate tender on Wednesday. A 14-day pact of 100 billion drachmas expires today.
"It's more of a correction on the upside than anything else," said a senior dealer. "Rates had eased too much."
Bond dealers said the secondary bond market was also calm and there was no follow up to an early expression of interest for buying FRNs.
"We had some queries for FRNs but there was no follow up," said a bond dealer at a private bank. "Prices are holding Tuesday afternoon levels."
Greece raised 208 billion drachmas from the sale of 12-month T-bills and two-year zeros according to provisional finance ministry figures.
T-bills carried a gross rate of 9.60 percent and two-year zeros a gross yield of 9.50 percent.
The mark was quoted at 157.50/55 from Tuesday's 157.370 fix, the dollar at 274.95/05 drachmas from 274.700 and the ecu at 309.43/53 from 309.31 drachmas.
"Ecu/drachma is firmer around 309.50 from 309.30 in quiet trading but we might see some pressure on the drachma due to the spillover effect from the devaluation of the baht."
A London-based bank trader said the float of the Thai baht, viewed by analysts as a de facto devaluation, might increase the risk premium for drachma investments.
